Effective line: Nurse Hesper hands you a cup of the Tea of Dissent. It is strong, bitter and entirely unapproved. HP restored.

Speaker: (narration)

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Ow! The Capital has hurt you again. (-HP)

Speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
Effective line: You wake up on a cot in the Crease. Nurse Hesper Dray is writing on a clipboard that, you notice, is blank on purpose.

Speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
Effective line: 'Dragged you in by the collar. Correction fee is yours. Drink. Then we can discuss your habit of arriving unconscious.'

Speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
Effective line: You wake in the dust outside the Approved Gate. A guard leans over you, measuring your height with a long stick.

Speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
Effective line: 'Falling in the approved queue area: minor offence. Fine payable. Stand up, citizen. I cannot measure you along the ground.'

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: A hidden stash! Someone hid this where {villain}'s inspectors would not look: behind something untidy.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You are through the walls. Somewhere a loudspeaker clears its throat. You are now, officially, a Visitor in {capital}, the Capital of {kingdom}.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The service-tunnel network is down. Nobody has run the wheels that power the shaft lifts in ten years. 'No travel,' says a Wrinkle's note on the hatch.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: 'Free the Gainlands and we will get the lifts turning.'

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You drop down the shaft, ride the lift through the dark and climb out somewhere else, smelling of rust.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You climb the ladder and push the manhole open. The Capital's cold light falls in.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You crawl out through the old tunnel and push the rubble aside. The Outskirts again, and a long way from anybody's approved queue.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You squeeze back down the collapsed shaft and follow the old tunnel in the dark.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You push past rubble and a toppled statue. You find stairs and read an old plaque: 'THE OLD JOINT WORKS. BUILT BY ALL FOUR PATHS, TOGETHER.'

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The tunnel runs under the wall, under the gate and under every one of {villain}'s checkpoints. You walk under them all. It is the best moment you have had all day.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You knock three times. The manhole opens to a hand and a tired voice: 'Down you come.'

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: A manhole by the wall, with a scratch on its lid like a tiny wrinkle. You knock three times, for no reason you can name.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: A pause. Then the lid lifts and a hand beckons. A voice mutters, 'Wrinkle?' You decide that, yes, you are.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Down a ladder, along a brick tunnel, into a warm room full of mismatched furniture and people who are all, visibly, not ironed.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You draw a moustache on {villain_title}'s portrait. A small coin drops from the frame: the Wrinkles' bounty for this improvement.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Already improved. He has a moustache now. He looks, for the first time, like a person.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You post a complaint. A coin drops from a slot with a note: 'Compensation for your inconvenience. Please use it to have less inconvenience.'

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You post a complaint. A hatch opens and a warm cup of tea is pushed out, still steaming. 'We value your concern,' says a note. You feel a little better.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You post a complaint. 'Noted,' says the box, gently. You wait. That appears to have been the whole service.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You post a complaint. A klaxon sounds. A Perfection Inspector appears from nowhere, measures your frown, writes you up and walks off.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: 'Thank you for your feedback,' says the box.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The box rattles. It is full. It has had enough of your feedback for one visit.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You set the rift-stone and say the old word: close. The tear shudders, folds in on itself like a letter, and is gone. The air smells of rain. Sealed!

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The rift-stone will not take while the rift's guardian still stands. Whatever it spat out has to go first.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The rift is sealed. Where it was there is a scorch mark and the memory of a very bad idea.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: This one is too big. It runs all the way up into the castle. It will have to close when he does.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: A real recipe, written by hand, with a stain of actual sauce on the corner! A pinch of this, a spoonful of that. It is wonderfully imprecise. You tuck it away.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: A banished compost heap, hiding in a cellar where it was not allowed to be. It is warm. It is alive.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: It steams, very slightly, with gratitude. Rescued!

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You unwrap a handkerchief and find a worn rubber stamp: FINAL APPROVAL. Someone hid it here, ready for the day it was needed.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: An old glass jar with one seed in it. The seed is glowing very faintly green. Nobody has planted anything in the Capital for ten years. It has not given up.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You already took the one lying here.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: There is nothing here.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The crew of the first wheel keeps running while you talk, because stopping is not permitted. 'Cardio,' pants a woman, 'is mandatory.' You find the brake lever under a pile of notices.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The wheel groans, slows and stops. The crew sit on the floor and laugh and cry at the same time.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The second wheel has been turning since before some of its runners were old enough to vote. A foreman's whistle hangs from a hook. You take it off its hook and put it in your pocket.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The wheel winds down. 'We were told,' says a man, 'that this was how you got strong.'

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The third wheel's crew are children. Children! 'It is a school activity,' says a banner.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You pull the lever, break the wheel's rhythm and get them off. They are very small and very proud and they will not stop saying 'Rollo sent you?'.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: This crew is free. They are lying on the ground, looking at the sky. It is the best they have felt in ten years.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You cut the big black cable that feeds the facade's lights from the wheels. A spark; a silence. Far off, the perfect lamps flicker, stutter and come back on: {villain} keeps a very small private generator, just for himself.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The cable is cut. The wires twitch occasionally, out of habit.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You pull the lever and ask the Perfect Nutrient Paste Dispenser for a refund. It chokes, burps and covers itself in a bright green foam that smells, fatally, of actual cabbage. A paste machine is not supposed to remember cabbage.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The dispenser is spoiled and sulking. The foam is still fizzing a little.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: With the Stamp of Final Approval pressed to the form, the grave plot's little iron gate unlocks. A line of mourners, who have waited three years outside, file in.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You watch the neighbourhood carry Mr. Pell to his grave. A quiet tune accompanies the coffin as they lower it.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The Pell plot is tended and quiet. Fresh flowers. The family comes every morning now.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The iron gate is sealed with a notice: 'NO BURIAL WITHOUT A STAMPED PERMIT (FORM 27-B/6, FINAL APPROVAL).' You have no stamp. Widow Pell said something about a stamp, hidden somewhere in Grave Row.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You kneel, scoop a hole with your hands and drop in the seed. You water it with what is left in your flask. Nothing happens, for one long, bad moment.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Then a shoot, as thin as a thread, noses out of the dirt. And another. And a flower, the colour of everything the Capital is not.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The patch is green and growing. A bee, which should not exist in the Capital, hovers over it, deciding.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The patch is sick, grey and cracked, and nothing will grow in it without a seed. Old Fern mentioned an old seed in a jar, hidden somewhere in the Reek.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The clerk behind the window slides you a form. 'For a burial permit, Form 27-B. Please attach Form 27-C (Proof of Grief).'

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You ask for 27-C. 'Please attach Form 27-B,' she says.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: 'Form 27-C requires Form 27-B.' 'Form 27-B requires Form 27-C.' 'It is a loop,' you say.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: 'It is a process,' she says, with fear in her eyes.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: 'Please take a number.' You take a number. It says 4,112,009.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The sign above the window says NOW SERVING: 3. It has said so for three years.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You read: 'Spontaneity Permits: Thursdays, 3:00 to 3:05, by appointment.' Inside, the clerk sleeps upright, eyes open.

Effective line: A Wrinkle is something that does not go away when you press it.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: THE WRINKLES

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Founded by people {villain} could not iron out. No dues. No forms. No smiling.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: THE SERVICE SHAFT NETWORK

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Built by all four Paths, together, back when we did that. Six shafts, six streets. (Beefcake wheels power the lifts. No wheels, no lifts.)

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: HOUSE RULES

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: 1. Say what you think.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: 2. Eat what you like. 3. Wear a hat of any size.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: 4. Do not tell anyone where we are.

Speaker: Wren
Effective line: Another one through the shafts. Sit. I am Wren. I was Royal Archivist, once. Now I keep the records this city is not supposed to have.

Speaker: Wren
Effective line: Maren sent word from {town} that someone might come. This is the Crease. We are the Wrinkles: the people {villain} could not iron out. We have tea and grudges. The tea is better.

Speaker: Wren
Effective line: He is in the castle at the north end, and he truly believes he is helping. That is the hard part. Talk to the streets. Each of them holds a piece of him.

Speaker: Wren
Effective line: Back in one piece? Good. Mostly one piece.

Speaker: Wren
Effective line: The records say he began as a good man. Keep that in mind. It does not excuse what he has done.

Speaker: Wren
Effective line: You brought me something from the streets. It goes in the true record, in ink, where he cannot correct it.

Speaker: Wren
Effective line: Two pieces of him now. A man who needs to be right. A man who cannot bear to be disagreed with. I can almost see his shape.

Speaker: Wren
Effective line: Three. He is afraid, you know. Not of you.

Speaker: Wren
Effective line: Of everything that will not obey. A small, sad fear, for a man with so much gold.

Speaker: Wren
Effective line: All four. I have the whole of him now. He is not a monster.

Speaker: Wren
Effective line: He is a man who made a list of everything he could not control, and made it illegal.

Speaker: Wren
Effective line: Go and finish it. Gently, if you can. But finish it.

Speaker: Fig Sly
When it's heard: Talking to Fig Sly (intro) [LOCKED: black market, never changed]
Effective line: Psst. Over here. Fig Sly, purveyor of contraband and curiosities.

Speaker: Fig Sly
When it's heard: Talking to Fig Sly (intro) [LOCKED: black market, never changed]
Effective line: Everything on this table is illegal, uneven or both.

Speaker: Fig Sly
When it's heard: Talking to Fig Sly (intro) [LOCKED: black market, never changed]
Effective line: Rare cards, good prices, no questions. Well: one question. Would you like a bag? Bags are illegal too.

Speaker: Fig Sly
When it's heard: Talking to Fig Sly (return) [LOCKED: black market, never changed]
Effective line: Back for more? Wise. Rare stock never lasts. Mind the one on the end: it bites.

Speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
Effective line: Hesper Dray. Nurse. Sit. Drink.

Speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
Effective line: Tea. Strong, bitter, unapproved. Drink while it is still three things the Ministry dislikes.

Speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
Effective line: The rifts? His hold is failing. Everything he forced together keeps coming apart, and he keeps stitching.

Speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
Effective line: It began the night the boy got out, they say. Nobody says 'boy' where the loudspeakers can hear.

Speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
Effective line: Bleeding again? Sit. I'll pretend to be surprised.

Speaker: Old Fern
Effective line: Shh. Keep it down. Old Fern. Composter.

Speaker: Old Fern
Effective line: I turned this city's waste back into soil. Now that's 'untidy', and so am I. Criminally untidy. Worms in my hat to prove it.

Speaker: Old Fern
Effective line: They shoved the rubbish behind the facade and called it 'Behind'. The land's sick. Nothing grows. Help me save what's left.

Speaker: Old Fern
Effective line: Any luck? The heaps are in cellars and holes all over the Reek. They think they're hiding. They're being rescued.

Speaker: Widow Pell
Effective line: Oh. A visitor. Forgive me, I've forgotten how this goes. I am Widow Pell. My husband died three years ago, in his chair in the front parlour.

Speaker: Widow Pell
Effective line: I cannot bury him. Form 27-B needs Form 27-C, and 27-C needs 27-B. He has waited in his chair for three years.

Speaker: Widow Pell
Effective line: I talk to him in the parlour. I don't know what else to do. Please, if you can help.

Speaker: Widow Pell
Effective line: The stamp, remember. Someone hid the Stamp of Final Approval where nobody official would look: somewhere in Grave Row, among papers nobody reads.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
Effective line: Rollo Spokes... foreman. Beefcake. Learned the wheels... in the Gainlands. Back then, a wheel stopped at night.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
Effective line: Now the facade needs light... so we pedal. Free. Forever. We were told... it was cardio. My calves have calves.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
Effective line: My crews run six hours a day... for ten years. Nobody's told them they can stop. Somebody ought to.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
Effective line: Three wheels... pull the brakes. And that big cable by the east wall... feeds the facade. Cut it.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
Effective line: The crews won't stop... till somebody says it's all right. You say it.

Speaker: Chef Marlo
Effective line: Hands where I can see them. Good. Chef Marlo. Once of the Market of the Four Paths. Now a 'Nutrient Distributor'. Recipes stay in my apron.

Speaker: Chef Marlo
Effective line: Everyone eats {villain}'s Perfect Nutrient Paste, three times a day. Paste is food the way a form is a hug.

Speaker: Chef Marlo
Effective line: For ten years I've hidden real recipes all over this quarter, so that somebody, somewhere, remembers what food is.

Speaker: Chef Marlo
Effective line: Three recipe cards, hidden in the quarter. And the dispenser: give it a good kick from me. Spoil it. Spoil it badly.

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Effective line: HALT. I am Captain Spotless. State your height.

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Effective line: No: do not state it. Stand at it. Straighter. Not that straight. APPROVED straight.

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Effective line: Entry requires the Approved Visitor Standard. You are too tall. You are too short. Your shadow is the wrong length.

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Effective line: However. The Standard has a provision: the Entry Examination. A card battle. Win it, and you are, retroactively, approved.

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Effective line: Do not look nervous. Nervousness is a Violation. (He polishes a button.) Shall we begin?

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Effective line: You again. Still too tall. Still smiling at the wrong angle. Ready for the Examination?

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Effective line: You are approved. I have always supported this outcome. Please remember that exact wording.

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Effective line: Please do not tell {villain_title} that I lost. Please do not tell anyone that I lost.

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Effective line: You are... approved. You are retroactively approved.

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Effective line: The Standard is satisfied. The gate opens, by order of the Standard and against my personal feelings.

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Effective line: I have measured eleven thousand visitors. I approved four. Nine thousand were sent home. The rest, I will not say.

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Effective line: Go through, citizen. In there, try not to be what you are.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro)
Effective line: Height inspection! Stand against the post. Straighten.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro)
Effective line: Not that straight. Hm. You are one hair above regulation.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro)
Effective line: One hair. I will let it go. This time. Do not grow.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (return)
Effective line: Still above regulation. Still letting it go. Do not make me regret it.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro)
Effective line: Queue management. The approved queue is this queue. You are in it.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro)
Effective line: You are not allowed to leave the queue. You are not allowed to join the queue. I do not understand it either.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (return)
Effective line: Still queueing? Good. You have a gift for remaining eligible.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (return)
Effective line: It is a long queue. It is the best queue we have.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro)
Effective line: Exit control. You are leaving? You have not arrived. Please arrive first.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (return)
Effective line: Exit control. Please have your exit permit ready. Please have your exit interview permit ready. Please have a reason.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro)
Effective line: Exit control. This is the exit. It is also the entrance. It is also, from some angles, a wall.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (return)
Effective line: Exit control. You are, I think, still inside. Congratulations.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro)
Effective line: Exit Interview Booth. Name? Reason for departing the most perfect place in the kingdom?

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro)
Effective line: 'It is not perfect' is not an approved answer. Nor is pointing at something while saying it.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (return)
Effective line: Your departure request has been received. It has been filed under 'Dissent'. It will be looked at in four to six years.

Speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
Effective line: Citizen 4471. I smiled incorrectly. Eleven degrees. The approved angle is eight.

Speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
Effective line: It was my wife's wedding. I had been crying. They corrected me.

Speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
Effective line: I do not smile any more. Not at all. It is a strange thing, to forget how a face works.

Speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
Effective line: I am improving, they say. I am not sure that is a good thing.

Speaker: (Quest Log)
When it's heard: Quest Log, "Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit": where to go (objective hint)
Effective line: Grave Row: the stamp lies north of the permit office

Speaker: (Quest Log)
When it's heard: Quest Log, "Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit": where to go (objective hint)
Effective line: The Pell family plot, at the north end of Grave Row

Speaker: (Quest Log)
When it's heard: Quest Log, "Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit": quest title
Effective line: Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit

Speaker: (Quest Log)
When it's heard: Quest Log, "Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit": quest summary
Effective line: Widow Pell's husband has sat in the family parlor for three years because his burial permit loops forever. It needs the Stamp of Final Approval, somewhere in Grave Row.

Speaker: (Quest Log)
When it's heard: Quest Log, "Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit": objective
Effective line: Find the Stamp of Final Approval in Grave Row

Speaker: (Quest Log)
When it's heard: Quest Log, "Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit": objective
Effective line: Lay Mr. Pell to rest at the family plot

Speaker: Widow Pell
When it's heard: Quest "Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit": when offered
Effective line: Please. A burial permit is all we want: Form 27-B/6, stamped Final Approval.

Speaker: Widow Pell
When it's heard: Quest "Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit": when offered
Effective line: Somebody hid the Stamp of Final Approval in Grave Row, among papers nobody reads. Find it, bring it to our family plot at the north end of Grave Row, and let him rest.

Speaker: Widow Pell
When it's heard: Quest "Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit": while it is active
Effective line: The stamp is somewhere in Grave Row, among papers nobody reads. Then the plot, at the north end of the Row. Please.

Speaker: Widow Pell
When it's heard: Quest "Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit": handing it in
Effective line: He's at rest? Oh. Oh.

Speaker: Widow Pell
When it's heard: Quest "Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit": handing it in
Effective line: I sat by the plot all morning and didn't say a word. It was the first quiet in three years that wasn't a fear.

Speaker: Widow Pell
When it's heard: Quest "Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit": handing it in
Effective line: Here. This was his. He'd want a young person to have it.

Speaker: Widow Pell
When it's heard: Quest "Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit": handing it in
Effective line: And something about the man in the castle. He schedules grief. Thursdays, 3:00 to 3:05. Anyone who cries outside those hours is corrected.

Speaker: Widow Pell
When it's heard: Quest "Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit": handing it in
Effective line: I don't think he is cruel. I think he simply cannot bear to watch.

Speaker: Widow Pell
When it's heard: Quest "Form 27-B/6: A Burial Permit": after it is done
Effective line: Thank you, a hundred times. We're at the plot every morning. What I told you is in your journal: he cannot stand a sadness he did not schedule.

Speaker: (Quest Log)
When it's heard: Quest Log, "The Wheel Never Stops": where to go (objective hint)
Effective line: The energy wheels along the Transit Yards wall

Speaker: (Quest Log)
When it's heard: Quest Log, "The Wheel Never Stops": where to go (objective hint)
Effective line: The main power cable, in the Transit Yards

Speaker: (Quest Log)
When it's heard: Quest Log, "The Wheel Never Stops": quest title
Effective line: The Wheel Never Stops

Speaker: (Quest Log)
When it's heard: Quest Log, "The Wheel Never Stops": quest summary
Effective line: Beefcake crews have run the facade's energy wheels for ten years because nobody told them they could stop. Go and tell them, in the Transit Yards.

Speaker: (Quest Log)
When it's heard: Quest Log, "The Wheel Never Stops": objective
Effective line: Free the wheel crews in the Transit Yards

Speaker: (Quest Log)
When it's heard: Quest Log, "The Wheel Never Stops": objective
Effective line: Cut the facade's power cable in the Yards

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
When it's heard: Quest "The Wheel Never Stops": when offered
Effective line: Three wheels in the Transit Yards... three crews nobody ever told to stop. Pull their brake levers... take the foreman's whistle... tell them it's all right.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
When it's heard: Quest "The Wheel Never Stops": when offered
Effective line: They won't believe you. Say it anyway. And cut the big cable by the east wall. The facade's lights have lived on my crews' legs for ten years.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
When it's heard: Quest "The Wheel Never Stops": while it is active
Effective line: Three wheels in the Transit Yards... free the crews. Cut the big cable by the east wall. Keep telling them they can stop.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
When it's heard: Quest "The Wheel Never Stops": handing it in
Effective line: Heard the lights flicker from here. Heard the crews sit down. The whole yard... quiet.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
When it's heard: Quest "The Wheel Never Stops": handing it in
Effective line: Haven't heard a quiet yard since the coup. Thank you.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
When it's heard: Quest "The Wheel Never Stops": handing it in
Effective line: Here. From the old days: what we gave people who could keep going.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
When it's heard: Quest "The Wheel Never Stops": handing it in
Effective line: And something about him. He made lateness illegal. A man who cannot wait for anyone.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
When it's heard: Quest "The Wheel Never Stops": handing it in
Effective line: Remember that when you meet him. He's always in a hurry... to be loved.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
When it's heard: Quest "The Wheel Never Stops": after it is done
Effective line: Wheels are slow. Crews are resting. What I said is in your journal: to him, lateness is disagreement, and disagreement is the one thing he won't forgive.

Speaker: (Quest Log)
When it's heard: Quest Log, "The Recipe Box": where to go (objective hint)
Effective line: Recipe cards hidden around the Hungry Quarter

Speaker: (Quest Log)
When it's heard: Quest Log, "The Recipe Box": where to go (objective hint)
Effective line: The paste dispenser, in the Hungry Quarter

Speaker: (Quest Log)
When it's heard: Quest Log, "The Recipe Box": quest title
Effective line: The Recipe Box

Speaker: (Quest Log)
When it's heard: Quest Log, "The Recipe Box": quest summary
Effective line: Everyone eats {villain}'s Perfect Nutrient Paste. Chef Marlo's three real recipes are hidden in the Hungry Quarter. Find them before the inspectors do.

Speaker: (Quest Log)
Effective line: Find Chef Marlo's recipe cards in the Hungry Quarter

Speaker: (Quest Log)
Effective line: Spoil the paste dispenser in the Hungry Quarter

Speaker: Chef Marlo
Effective line: Three of my recipes are hidden in the Hungry Quarter: a bread, a stew, a sauce. Real ones, in my hand, quantities written as 'some'. Find them before the inspectors do.

Speaker: Chef Marlo
Effective line: And the paste dispenser by the east wall: spoil it. Give it a very bad day.

Speaker: Chef Marlo
When it's heard: Quest "The Recipe Box": while it is active
Effective line: Three recipe cards in the Hungry Quarter, and the dispenser to spoil. 'Some' of this, 'a bit' of that. Always a good recipe.

Speaker: Chef Marlo
When it's heard: Quest "The Recipe Box": handing it in
Effective line: The bread! The stew! The sauce!

Speaker: Chef Marlo
When it's heard: Quest "The Recipe Box": handing it in
Effective line: Look at the stains. Look at the spelling. And that smell from the dispenser: cabbage. Real cabbage.

Speaker: Chef Marlo
When it's heard: Quest "The Recipe Box": handing it in
Effective line: I am crying. Let me. Here: my real recipe, the one I never dared write down until today.

Speaker: Chef Marlo
When it's heard: Quest "The Recipe Box": handing it in
Effective line: And something about him. He cannot taste. Not food, not wine, not salt. He never could.

Speaker: Chef Marlo
When it's heard: Quest "The Recipe Box": handing it in
Effective line: He built a whole kingdom of paste because he could not understand what the rest of us were missing.

Speaker: Chef Marlo
When it's heard: Quest "The Recipe Box": after it is done
Effective line: I'm cooking again. Real food, real mess. What I told you is in your journal: he made everyone eat what he could not taste.

Speaker: (Quest Log)
When it's heard: Quest Log, "Untidy": where to go (objective hint)
Effective line: Banished heaps hide in the Reek's cellars and yards

Speaker: (Quest Log)
When it's heard: Quest Log, "Untidy": where to go (objective hint)
Effective line: The Sick Patch in the Reek. Find the jar of old seed first

Speaker: (Quest Log)
Effective line: Untidy

Speaker: (Quest Log)
Effective line: Composting is outlawed as untidy, and the land is sickening for it. Three banished compost heaps are hiding in the Reek. Rescue them.

Speaker: (Quest Log)
Effective line: Rescue the banished compost heaps in the Reek

Speaker: (Quest Log)
Effective line: Plant the old seed in the Sick Patch

Speaker: Old Fern
Effective line: Three compost heaps are hiding in the Reek, in cellars and under floors, where they were told to wait. Rescue them. They're alive.

Speaker: Old Fern
Effective line: And there's an old seed in a jar somewhere nearby. Plant it in the Sick Patch, in the Reek. Nobody's planted a thing here in ten years.

Speaker: Old Fern
Effective line: Three compost heaps and one jarred seed in the Reek. Rescue the heaps. Plant the seed in the Sick Patch. Give it a chance.

Speaker: Old Fern
Effective line: It took? It TOOK. A flower. In this city.

Speaker: Old Fern
Effective line: I need to sit down. I need to sit down and smell it.

Speaker: Old Fern
Effective line: Here. Take it. And something about him: he's afraid of anything that grows without asking him first.

Speaker: Old Fern
Effective line: Weeds. Moss. Children. Anything that surprises him. I think that's the whole of him.

Speaker: Old Fern
Effective line: Patch is blooming. Heaps are steaming. What I said is in your journal: he's afraid of anything that grows on its own.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: Good day! The weather is approved! The lawn is regulation!

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: Everything is perfect, and I am so, so pleased about it.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: Good day! It is a very good day. It is the same day as yesterday.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: That is also good. That is the best.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: Everything is perfect. Everything is... (a pause, then a whisper) ...please do not tell the Inspector I blinked.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: Welcome to {showcase}! Houses, lawns, a small round approved fountain. Everything you could want. Everything you may want.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: The bread is lovely. The bread is... (a fixed smile) I have a permit for four more words. I wish it existed.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: I had a name before. I think it started with a B. I am allowed to forget it. I am doing very well at it.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: My house is identical to my neighbour's! Is that not wonderful? There is nothing to envy, and nothing to be envied for.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: Isn't it lovely to be exactly the same? I used to be different. I do not remember why. It sounds very tiring.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: Sometimes I go behind the house and look at the wall. Just the wall. Nobody has told me I cannot. Please do not tell them.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: Smile! That is all there is to it! Smiling is mandatory, and I am, in my opinion, a very good smiler.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: Seventy percent, minimum! I am at seventy-one! It is a good day.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: My cheeks hurt. Please do not tell anyone my cheeks hurt.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: The man next door smiled at his wife's funeral. He was remembering her laugh.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: (a whisper) They corrected him for a month. He does not remember her laugh now.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: The hedge is square! The hedges are all square! I trim the hedge every morning, to make sure it is as square as yesterday's.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: The Showcase receives visitors from all over! (a pause) Nobody visits. Nobody has visited in six years. We still smile in case they do.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: Do you hear the loudspeaker? It plays the same thing every day. It has said my name once.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: Once. I wish it would again.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: Spontaneity is only for Thursdays! Today is Wednesday! I am almost allowed to be excited!

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: Thursday! Five minutes of spontaneity, permit ready! I have rehearsed being caught off guard.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: I tried to be spontaneous once. On a Tuesday. I said 'hello' to a bird.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: I was corrected for two weeks. (a whisper) I still think about that bird.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: Your hat is of an unapproved size, but I will not mention it, because that would be impolite. I am so, so polite. I am the politest person in the Showcase.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: Approved Hat Size: 1. I wear the one. It is a good hat. I do not know whose it is.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: My daughter had a green hat. A little green hat. They said it was a Disagreement.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: I do not know where the hat is. I do not know where my daughter is. Everything is perfect.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: The Showcase is the best of all possible places! I would not live anywhere else! (looking at the exit) ...I would not be allowed to.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: Everyone is so friendly! Everyone is so friendly. It is like living inside a greeting card.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: There is a door at the back that does not open. I think there is a world on the other side. I think it is raining.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: {villain_title} is so kind. He loves us all, and he made everything this way, for us. For our own good. (a shake) For our own good.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: The portrait is looking at me. It is always looking at me. It is very kind of him to look.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: I would never look away. I cannot.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: He is not here. He has never been here. The portraits are here.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: The portraits do all the looking. It is all done by portrait.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: You try the front door. It does not open. It is not a door.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: It is a very well-painted rectangle on a wall. Somebody has painted a tiny brass knocker. You knock on it.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: It makes a sound like knocking on a wall.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: You try the door. It does not open. You peek through the window: it is a painting of a window, and beyond it a painting of a living room with a painting of a family.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: They are smiling. They have been smiling for six years.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: The door has no handle. The house has no inside. Behind the facade there is just room for a ladder and a young woman painting the same window for the thousandth time.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: She looks at you. She looks away. She has the face of someone who has meant to write home for years.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: You try the door. It is open! It is a closet.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: It contains a mop, a bucket and a sign that says: IF YOU ARE READING THIS, SMILE.

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Effective line: Attention, citizens! Today is a PERFECT day! The weather is APPROVED!

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Effective line: Please continue to be happy, as scheduled! This has been your Deputy Minister of Good News!

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Effective line: Attention, citizens! A reminder that smiling is MANDATORY! Those found frowning will be helped! Thank you for your cooperation!

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
